transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-08-25 15:00 UTC | Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Daniel Park (Redwood SE), Ravi Patel (VectorGrid - Head of Partnerships), Laura Kim (VectorGrid - Cloud Architect), Omar Ruiz (VectorGrid - Director, GTM)

Auto-summary: Intro partner discovery. VectorGrid is a cloud/GPU distribution partner exploring integrated resale and joint go-to-market; primary concerns are VPC peering, data residency, and predictable latency for realtime use-cases.

---
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Maya from Redwood, AE on the partnerships team. With me is Daniel our SE. Quick intros?
[00:18] Ravi: Hi yeah Ravi here, head of partnerships at VectorGrid. We run a global GPU cloud for inference workloads and want to explore reseller + technology integration with Redwood.
[00:28] Laura: Laura, cloud architect - we manage peering, networking, and compliance on our side.
[00:34] Omar: Omar, I run GTM. Interested in how we can co-sell and packaging options.
[00:40] Daniel: Awesome. Real quick agenda: partnership model, technical integration options (hosted API vs dedicated vs private), security requirements, then next steps. Any additions?
[00:50] Ravi: Sounds good. Also want to understand pricing flex and what benchmarking you'd need.

[01:05] Maya: Great. To start, high level, Redwood offers a hosted API, Redwood Dedicated (reserved GPU pools), and Redwood Private (VPC / on-prem). For partners like you we typically do two things: 1) resell/managed offering where you host infra and surface Redwood's control plane or 2) joint referrals with integrations for VPC peering and identity.
[01:28] Laura: Quick clarifying q: when you say "hosted API" are customer payloads leaving VectorGrid or staying in our VPC?
[01:36] Daniel: Good call. Hosted API means traffic goes to Redwood's hosted infra, payloads transit our control plane. For stricter data residency and isolation we offer Redwood Dedicated (you could run in our dedicated pools) or Redwood Private, where we deploy a private control plane in your VPC or on-prem so data never leaves your network.
[01:56] Ravi: Okay so Private is the path for our enterprise customers that require no egress. Any examples of VPC peering or direct connect?
[02:03] Daniel: Yes, we support VPC peering and private link-style setups; we've also done private control planes with HSM/KMS integrations. There might be some subtle infra work we'll share a sample architecture.

[02:18] Laura: On compliance, we need SOC 2 and ISO readiness. Do you have audit logs and RBAC?
[02:24] Maya: Yes, we are SOC 2 with audit logs, RBAC and SSO/SAML integrations. We also support customer-managed KMS and HSM for key storage for Private deployments. We'll share the security pack link.

[02:40] Ravi: Perfect. On the technical side: our customers need consistent 99ms p95 for short-turnaround chat. Do you have latency SLOs? How do you handle batching vs single-request latency?
[02:53] Daniel: We have latency profiles per model and deployment mode. Hosted API optimizes for low median latency with continuous batching; Dedicated lets you reserve capacity for predictable throughput. For sub-100ms p95, often we edge route to dedicated pools with smaller batch windows and KV cache priming. We also recommend quantization for cost but depends on model.
[03:17] Laura: What GPUs do you support? H100/A100? Any talk of Gaudi?
[03:22] Daniel: We run a mix H100 for high perf, A100 for common throughput. We've worked with partners on Gaudi too. GPU selection is part of the Dedicated sizing conversation.

[03:40] Omar: From a GTM perspective, what does partnership look like? Revenue share? Co-selling?
[03:45] Maya: Typical models: reseller (you host and resale), referral fee, or co-sell with joint SKUs. We usually start with a pilot to validate performance and then a commercial agreement.
[03:56] Ravi: For pilots, what telemetry do you need? We want to be sure customer observability is maintained.
[04:02] Daniel: We emit token-level cost and latency breakdowns, per-route dashboards, tracing hooks, and error analysis. For private deployments we can forward logs to your logging endpoint or ship logs to your SIEM.

[04:20] [crosstalk] Laura: (quiet) can you show a sample dashboard?
[04:25] Maya: We'll share screenshots and the console walkthrough - link in follow up.

[04:30] Ravi: On integration friction: how heavy is the engineering lift for a Private deployment? We've got limited SRE resources right now.
[04:38] Daniel: Private can be heavier up-front for network and key management. We provide an install package and can run the onboarding jointly. Dedicated is generally simpler if you can host within our partner-managed pools and do SSO. For minimal lift, many partners start with a hybrid: host Dedicated nodes in your DC but manage the control plane together.

[05:00] Omar: Any known blockers around billing or metering when partners host infra?
[05:05] Maya: We support usage reporting export and invoice aggregation. For partner-hosted models we can do monthly settlement or pass-through billing. We'll need to align on metering semantics (token counts, embeddings, etc.).

[05:22] Ravi: Security follow-ups: do you support customer-managed certificates and private CA?
[05:27] Daniel: Yes, customer-managed certs, private CA, mutual TLS are supported in Private mode. Also SSO via SAML and SCIM for provisioning.

[05:40] Laura: Regarding model/versioning and rollouts: can we pin model versions and run canary rollouts?
[05:46] Maya: Absolutely. Rollouts, canary, A/B, automatic fallback policies these are in the Console. We can also tie quality monitoring to prompt sets.

[06:00] Ravi: Benchmarks: what would you need to do a quick perf estimate for a pilot?
[06:06] Daniel: A few things: model family, typical sequence length, tokens per request, concurrency targets, and latency SLO. If you give example prompts we can run a small benchmark suite against our Dedicated config to produce cost/latency numbers.

[06:22] Omar: Ok, rough ask: 50 concurrent sessions, avg 128 tokens, target p95 < 150ms. Can you ballpark cost?
[06:30] Daniel: We'll put together a pilot costing; rough order of magnitude depends on model and quantization. We'll follow up with a spreadsheet.

[06:40] [pause]
[06:45] Maya: A few implementation details to raise: do you want our control plane embedded into your portal, or do you prefer a white-label approach?
[06:53] Omar: White-label would be ideal for our enterprise reseller customers.
[06:57] Maya: Great, that's supported  we can provide a private control plane and embed console parts or offer API-only flows.

[07:10] Laura: Networking nit: can we do IP allow lists + peering and keep logs within our SIEM?
[07:16] Daniel: Yes, we'll document forwarding logs, IP ranges, and peering setup.

[07:25] Ravi: Any red flags from partner experience?
[07:29] Maya: Biggest is alignment on support SLAs and ownership matrix. We recommend a runbook: who owns incident response, who escalates, and how billing disputes are handled. We'll include a template.

[07:42] Omar: Let's talk timelines. We have enterprise pilot opportunities in Q4. What does your onboarding typically look like?
[07:50] Daniel: Onboarding varies: Hosted API can be done in days; Dedicated/Pilot with benchmarking and Private setup is usually 4-8 weeks depending on network approvals. For partners we compress that by running parallel legal/security work.

[08:07] Ravi: Legal/compliance: we need a template SLA and DPA. Do you have those or do we need to draft?
[08:12] Maya: We have templates. We'll attach DPA and standard MSA redlines; for Private deployments we often add SOC2 attestation language.

[08:25] Daniel: Quick technical detail  our runtime supports continuous batching, KV cache for prefix caching (sometimes transcribed as KV cash), and quantization-friendly execution. For realtime chat use-cases we tune batch windows and pre-prime KV cache to hit latency SLOs.

[08:45] Laura: Is there a recommended quantization profile for 8-bit vs 4-bit?
[08:50] Daniel: Depends on the model. For Llama-family style models, 4-bit quantization often gets you good cost savings with minimal quality regression for many tasks. We'll recommend per-model profiles in the Optimize toolkit.

[09:05] Ravi: Any integrations required for billing or usage?
[09:09] Maya: We'll exchange an integration checklist; standard is a metering endpoint and optionally a usage reporting S3 export.

[09:18] Omar: From a GTM perspective, co-marketing assets  do you have partner collateral?
[09:23] Maya: Yes, we'll share a partner one-pager, joint case study template, and PR guidelines.

[09:30] Laura: One more compliance q: do you support customer-managed KMS in cloud partners?
[09:36] Daniel: Yes  customer-managed KMS is available for Private and Dedicated in many cases; for Hosted we offer envelope encryption with Redwood-managed keys unless otherwise negotiated.

[09:50] [background noise]
[09:56] Maya: Okay wrapping toward next steps: we'll send the partner one-pager, security docs, sample VPC arch, and a benchmark request template. VectorGrid to confirm technical deep dive availability.
[10:12] Ravi: We'll get internal signoff and share network diagrams by next week.
[10:18] Omar: I'll coordinate GTM contacts and share potential pilot customers.
[10:23] Maya: Perfect. Any other open questions?
[10:28] Laura: Not for now, thanks.
[10:30] Maya: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the links.
